training_data: SYNTHETIC: sessions from the seeded scenario simulator in models/build_model.py, labelled by the explicit window teacher documented there. Not real telemetry or incident data.

input.name: features
input.semantics: channel = feature (models/feature_schema.json order), width = last 64 events of one session, oldest -> newest, zero-padded on the left

output.name: risk_score
output.semantics: risk of the newest event given the session history in the window

architecture.name: mh128_b5_v8_nd
architecture.description: x * horizon_mask -> 8 views on the height axis (horizons [64, 48, 32, 24, 16, 8, 4, 1]); 1x1 stem conv; 5 residual blocks relu(h + conv1x1(relu(conv1x3(h)))), undilated (dilation 1 in every block); newest-position receptive field 11 events; readout concat(newest position, mean over width) per view -> (8 x 1) conv -> relu -> 1x1 conv -> sigmoid x 100

precision: float16 weights, activations, input and output (ML Program, macOS 14 opset)

latency_at_build.note: aegis_ane_score_windows through the production Swift bridge, one full window per prediction, .cpuAndNeuralEngine and .cpuOnly interleaved in alternating rounds on a shared machine; preliminary, a quiet benchmark is authoritative

batch_model.semantics: same weights as the online model; scores BATCH independent sessions per prediction (one per batch entry, aegis_input_layout=window_batch). AneScorer::score_batch(vectors) scores every vector as a session with no history, identical to AneScorer::score; AneScorer::score_windows scores whole sessions.

teacher.event: feature_schema.json weights + interactions, slope/bias (phase-1 teacher) on the newest event

validation.scored_by: PyTorch FP32 reference: forward pass of the trained weights in torch float32, not the shipped FP16 CoreML model (see validation_coreml_fp16 for that)

validation_coreml_fp16.scored_by: AegisWorkflowFP16.mlpackage: shipped CoreML FP16 ML Program, coremltools predict, .cpuAndNeuralEngine, same held-out windows as validation

parity.reference: PyTorch FP32 forward pass of the trained weights

history_probes.description: History-only payment velocity: one order (commerce features only, orders_last_hour and spend_last_24h_cents 0) repeated N times in one session; parity_vectors.json history_probes holds the events. Scored by the shipped FP16 model (.cpuAndNeuralEngine) and the PyTorch FP32 reference; teacher is the window teacher label.

architecture_sweep.description: Architecture sweep for the online window model. Each candidate is built with seeded random (He) weights; MLComputePlan placement and latency do not depend on weight values for dense FP16 convolutions, and the final trained model is re-measured by the full build. Latency is the wall-clock time of aegis_ane_score_windows through the production Swift bridge (models/tools/ane_probe.swift), .cpuAndNeuralEngine and .cpuOnly interleaved in alternating rounds. Measured on a shared machine: preliminary numbers.

selection_rule.order: fewest MACs per window, then fewest parameters, among passing rows

limitations: Training data is synthetic and the labels come from a hand-written teacher; the model has not been validated on real agent sessions or incidents.
Scores are only as meaningful as the feature extraction feeding them.
Neural Engine placement and the ANE-vs-CPU latency ratio were measured on one Apple M2; MLComputePlan decides placement per machine and OS.
